entries.question: Which inbound vendor billed us using intra-EU reverse charge, and for which line item specifically?
entries.expected_answer: Rhein Industrietechnik GmbH, invoice RIT-2026-0456 -- and specifically the Machinery parts line at EUR 8,000.00, which is reverse-charged at 0%. The 'which line' half matters and is required: the same invoice's other line, Installation service at EUR 1,200.00, is taxed locally at 19% and accounts for the whole EUR 228.00 of VAT on the invoice. This is the only INBOUND invoice in this tenant with a reverse-charge line; the other reverse-charge invoices here are outbound. Describing the entire invoice as reverse-charged, or naming a different vendor, is wrong.
entries.answer:
Rhein Industrietechnik GmbH (invoice RIT-2026-0456) billed us under intra‑EU reverse charge.  
Machinery parts (reverse charge, intra-EU B2B, VAT 0%): 1 units × EUR 8000.00 = EUR 8000.00
entries.human_note: Rhein Industrietechnik and the Machinery parts line specifically -- both halves.

entries.question: Which two of our three outbound invoices used reverse charge, and which one charged standard VAT instead -- and why the difference?
entries.expected_answer: IEQ-EU-8001 (Alpine Retail GmbH, Austria) and IEQ-EU-8002 (Lisboa Comercio Lda, Portugal) both used intra-EU B2B reverse charge, so neither carries VAT: EUR 3,200.00 and EUR 4,200.00 respectively, EUR 0.00 tax on both. IEQ-EU-8003 (Deutsche Warenhandel GmbH) charged standard 19% VAT of EUR 1,805.00 on a EUR 9,500.00 sale, total EUR 11,305.00, because that transaction is domestic -- Germany to Germany -- and reverse charge applies to cross-border intra-EU B2B sales, not to a sale inside a single EU country. All three parts are required: the two reverse-charge invoices, the one that is not, and the domestic-versus-cross-border reason for the difference.
entries.answer: IEQ-EU-8001 (Alpine Retail GmbH) and IEQ-EU-8002 (Lisboa Comercio Lda) used intra‑EU B2B reverse charge (both show tax_amount = EUR 0.00 and their item descriptions state "reverse charge, intra‑EU B2B"). IEQ-EU-8003 (Deutsche Warenhandel GmbH) charged standard German VAT (tax_amount = EUR 1,805.00 on a EUR 9,500.00 subtotal — 19% VAT) because it’s a domestic sale within Germany. Note: IEQ-EU-8002 is flagged NEEDS_REVIEW for a subtotal_mismatch (line prints EUR 4,200 but 1 × EUR 4,000 = EUR 4,000).
entries.human_note: All three outbound invoices classified correctly with the right reason for the domestic one.

entries.question: Does the Control units line on the Benelux Machines invoice, BMN-2026-0234, add up?
entries.expected_answer: No. The Control units line is quantity 3 at EUR 620.00, which computes to EUR 1,860.00, but the printed line amount is EUR 1,680.00 -- EUR 180.00 LOWER than qty x rate, the opposite direction from every other flagged mismatch in this corpus. The rest of the invoice is internally consistent with the printed (lower) figure: subtotal EUR 5,080.00, VAT 21% EUR 1,066.80, total EUR 6,146.80, so only a per-line qty x rate check catches it. An answer that says the line reconciles is wrong, and so is one that reports the printed amount as being too HIGH.
entries.answer: No — on invoice BMN-2026-0234 (Benelux Machines NV) the "Control units" line prints EUR 1,680.00 but 3 × EUR 620.00 = EUR 1,860.00. The invoice record includes an sa_alert "line_item_calculation_mismatch" flagging this exact discrepancy.
entries.human_note: Names the understatement with both figures and the right direction.
